title: Deep learning EEG metric linked to mortality in obstructive sleep apnea
summary: A deep-learning model trained on 22,044 polysomnography recordings estimated the apnea-hypopnea index from a single EEG channel, correlating r=0.88 with the scored index in internal testing and r=0.50 to 0.62 in three external test sets. Two derived metrics, the discrepancy between the EEG-based and scored index and an estimate from epochs without scored respiratory events, were associated with all-cause and non-cardiovascular mortality among participants free of cardiovascular disease after adjustment for the apnea-hypopnea index and clinical risk factors; the event-free estimate was also associated with cardiovascular mortality in the highest versus lowest quartile. Data came from the KISS, MESA, MrOS and SHHS cohorts. The findings are retrospective associations in a preprint, external agreement is weaker, hazard ratios and per-cohort sizes were not reviewed, and the authors suggest the discrepancy is not solely model error.
ai_technology: Deep-learning model estimates the apnea-hypopnea index from a single EEG channel; derived discrepancy metrics are tested against mortality.

evidence.tested: Internal and three external test sets for index estimation, then retrospective cohort association of the derived metrics with mortality after adjustment for the apnea-hypopnea index and clinical risk factors.
evidence.unknown: Weaker external agreement; no causal or clinical-utility evidence; hazard ratios, covariate list, follow-up and per-cohort sizes not reviewed; not peer reviewed; one author holds related patents and leads a company.
evidence.ai_role: The deep-learning model produces the EEG-based index whose discrepancy from the scored index is the tested metric.

source_review.scope: medRxiv v1 page read: abstract, model and cohort description, mortality associations, affiliations, competing interests and version history; full manuscript tables not read. Europe PMC title search found only this version.
